- [USER] User requested a short summary on Herod the Great.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Herod the Great was a king of Judea, who ruled from 37 BCE to 4 BCE, known for his ambitious building projects and ruthless tactics.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Herod was the son of Antipater the Idumaean, appointed king by the Roman Senate.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Herod is known for the renovation of the Second Temple in Jerusalem and the construction of the port city of Caesarea Maritima.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] He is also known for the slaughter of the innocents, a mass killing of male children in Bethlehem to kill the newborn Jesus.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Despite his controversial reign, Herod is considered one of the greatest rulers in Jewish history for his military victories, administrative skills, and cultural achievements.
- [USER] User asked about Herod's origin.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Herod was of Edomite origin, as his father Antipater was an Edomite, a member of a group descended from Esau.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Herod was accepted by the Jewish people as their ruler despite his Edomite origins.
- [USER] User inquired how Herod became king.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Herod became king of Judea in 37 BCE after being appointed by the Roman Senate.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] He gained favor from the Roman Senate and general Marcus Licinius Crassus, which supported his bid for the throne.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Herod was appointed king after the defeat of the last Hasmonean ruler, Antigonus II Mattathias.
